style.vernacular: Central European city of layered periods: a compact Old Town of 14th-18th century Gothic and Baroque houses and palaces in pastel plaster (ochre, salmon, cream, pale green) under steep red clay-tile roofs; 19th-century neoclassical and Secession blocks; and, across the Danube in Petrzalka and in Dubravka, Karlova Ves and Ruzinov, vast communist-era prefabricated concrete panel housing estates (panelaky) of 8-13 storeys, often repainted in pastel insulation colours. Glass-and-steel offices, malls and towers from the 2000s stand along the river. Villages around the city (Stupava, Cunovo, Samorin) have low plastered houses with hip roofs and small Baroque churches.
style.ornament: Baroque plaster facades with white window surrounds and cornices, steep tile roofs with dormers, Rococo and neoclassical palaces (Grassalkovich), Plague Column (1713) squares; panelak facades with coloured balcony bands and loggias; the single-pylon SNP bridge with its UFO deck as the modern emblem.

sources.what: Old Town with medieval/Baroque buildings (Town Hall 14th-15th c., Michael's Gate, Grassalkovich Palace, Plague Column 1713); prefabricated panel high-rises in Petrzalka and Dubravka; 21st-century towers
